title: Knock it down: a character throws things at breakable scenery against a clock
summary: A walker carries and throws balls at fracturable kit parts; every piece knocked out of place is a point; reach the score before time runs out. Covers demolition, target throwing, a snowball fight against a fort, bowling-like games.
applies_when: the player controls a character on foot who carries, throws or kicks an object
the targets are scenery that breaks into pieces or falls over, and points come from what was knocked down
the round ends by reaching a score or by a time limit
not_when: targets shoot back or move with intent (needs enemy AI the seed does not show)
the thing thrown must be caught or passed between characters

data_files.role: the venue: the breakable props with ids the script finds by prefix, the spawn point, scenery, a fixed camera
the score that wins and the time limit
walker speeds, the ball pool, throw speed and angle, block toughness, camera

do: Use fracturable kit parts (barrier_wall, crate) as targets and attach TLFracture to each; the kit already prepared the pieces.
Let impacts do the damage: a TLBall reports its hits and the block's damage model does the arithmetic; tune hp and threshold, write no damage code.
Check that the thrown object can hurt the target at all: impulse is mass times speed and must exceed the material's threshold.
Queue events in signal handlers and act on the queue as the last step of _pack_tick.
Score pieces by how far they moved from their place, so the count means knocked down and not cracked.
Play rig clips from game events (carry, cheer) and mark breaks with one effect burst and one sound.
dont: Do not build targets from script boxes: they would not fracture and would not wear the style.
Do not subtract health in the script on contact: TLDamage already does, from the real impulse.
Do not create the next ball inside the release or the break handler: do it in _pack_tick.
Do not let the rules say over before the pack reacted (HUD text, horn): the bot reads both.
Do not set score_to_win above what the bot knocks down with margin: measure first (the seed's bot gets 40 to 45 pieces).

bot.plays_by: the player's own actions only: it lines up with the nearest standing block at throwing distance, faces it and throws whenever it holds a ball; too close, it walks out and comes in again.
bot.wins_when: the rules say state over with reason score, the HUD shows the win text, one break sound per broken block and one horn were recorded; reason time fails.

acceptance: The bot wins by score, never by time, at seeds 1 to 3.
A player who never throws loses by time with a score of 0.
Every block can break: none has hp or threshold beyond what the thrown object delivers.
Lint reports 0 bypasses and 0 kit parts added.
The orbit camera keeps the walker and the targets in frame; HUD shows score and clock.

variants.change: the same release with a flat velocity from the feet; lower the hold offset.
params of the block props in yard.json; raise score_to_win only after re-measuring the bot.

variants.ask: crates or a tower instead of a wall
variants.change: swap barrier_wall for crate (also fracturable) stacked by layout transforms.
lower the blocks' threshold with the ball's mass or nothing breaks (8 kg at 19 m/s is about 150 N*s; concrete's default threshold is 260).
